issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Ride: The problem statement and UML require Ride to have a public constructor accepting both attributes (String name, char abbreviation) in that order (problem_statement.md lines 5 and UML lines 21-24). In the solution (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) Ride only declares public Ride(String name) and assigns a default abbreviation, while RollerCoaster (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java) defines a constructor public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) and calls super(name, abbreviation). This mismatch means subclasses that follow the UML/specified constructor ordering cannot compile against the provided Ride implementation and will confuse students implementing subclass constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Ride constructor with the UML and problem statement by adding a public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) constructor that assigns both fields. Update the class to keep that constructor (or overload it) so subclasses can call super(name, abbreviation). Ensure all subclass constructors accept superclass attributes first (name, abbreviation) followed by subclass attributes (e.g., numberOfLoopings) as specified.
